description: Machine-readable terminology dictionary for Stigmer documentation. The terminology linter reads this file to enforce consistent use of ubiquitous language across all docs.

terms.context: A portable, versioned, declarative definition of an AI worker. The proto resource in the agentic domain.
A single invocation of an agent instance within a session. Produces messages, tool calls, and results.
Binds an Agent blueprint to an environment — provides secrets, credentials, and runtime values.
Groups related AgentExecutions into a conversational context. Maintains message history across multiple runs.
A portable, versioned, content-addressed package of domain knowledge injected into an agent's context at runtime.
A portable, versioned, declarative definition of a durable automation pipeline with typed task steps.
A single run of a WorkflowInstance. Backed by Temporal for durability.
Binds a Workflow blueprint to an environment, similar to how AgentInstance binds an Agent.
A portable, versioned tool integration definition following the Model Context Protocol. Exposes tools and resources to agents.
The root namespace for all Stigmer resources. Every resource belongs to exactly one Organization.
exceptions: 'org' is permitted in CLI flag names (--org), YAML fields (metadata.org), and inline code references

terms.context: An encrypted key-value store that provides secrets and configuration to AgentInstances and WorkflowInstances.
exceptions: 'env' is permitted in CLI flag names (--env), YAML fields, and technical references to environment variables

terms.context: A managed grouping of related resources with orphan pruning. Created by stigmer apply from a Stigmer.yaml.
A git repository or local path that serves as an agent's working directory during execution.
A complete Stigmer project embedded in the CLI binary containing system agents, skills, and MCP servers that bootstrap every install.
The Python service that executes AI agents using LangGraph with MCP server integration, skill injection, and checkpoint-based state management.
The Go service that interprets CNCF Serverless Workflow definitions, executing HTTP calls, gRPC calls, agent invocations, and control flow tasks.
The canonical principal type in the IAM domain. Represents a human or machine identity.
exceptions: 'user' is permitted when referring to a generic person in non-technical prose (e.g., 'the user clicks the button')

terms.context: A declarative access grant that binds a principal to a permission on a resource.
Enables federated authentication so external platforms can let their users access Stigmer without a separate account.
A managed programmatic credential for API access.
exceptions: 'token' is permitted when referring to LLM tokens (prompt tokens, completion tokens) or Temporal auth tokens

terms.context: An ephemeral runtime secret bundle assembled from Environment entries for a specific execution.
The Go gRPC server that owns every API resource and coordinates execution.
exceptions: 'server' is permitted in CLI commands (stigmer server start) and when referring to generic server concepts

terms.context: The CLI command that deploys resources from YAML or Go code to the Stigmer backend.
exceptions: 'deploy' is permitted when referring to the general concept of deployment, not the specific Stigmer command

terms.context: The CLI command that creates an AgentExecution or WorkflowExecution.
exceptions: 'execute' and 'invoke' are permitted in general programming contexts, not when referring to the specific CLI command
